strings.meta.home: Search a ZIP code for nearby open-burning and open-detonation munitions sites, military PFAS sites, EPA Superfund sites and FUSRAP nuclear cleanup sites, or browse regional sections. Built from official records. Not an official government document. By D.A. Williams.
strings.site.cover_alt: Dark photo collage titled Dangerous Munitions Near Me. In the center, a real munitions-disposal explosion with a fireball and smoke. Around it are photographs of a Caution Radioactive Materials warning sign, leaking hazardous-waste drums, an aerial view of the Church Rock uranium mine on the Navajo Nation, a Danger Unexploded Ordnance sign, sailors wading through military firefighting foam, and a coral-encrusted sea-dumped munition. A Search your ZIP label sits under the title, and a graphic threat-level scale along the bottom is labeled as not an official military alert.
strings.site.hero_credit_html: Cover photograph credits are listed on the About / methods page.
strings.footer.byline: By D.A. Williams. Not an official government document.
strings.legend.marker_note: Larger dots have a deeper research note in this inventory. Marker color is the verification label. Coordinates come from EPA FRS, not from hand-placed guesses.

strings.home.mission: A worldwide, source-linked record of places harmed or put at risk by military munitions, nuclear weapons and energy, chemical weapons and industrial disasters. It spans every continent and both poles, with layers for military bases and firing ranges, unexploded wartime bombs, nuclear test, accident and waste sites, chemical weapons stockpiles and sea dumps, chemical-plant and petroleum disasters, and mine-waste and coal-ash dam failures. Records link to their sources — official government, treaty and court documents wherever available — and each is marked verified, corrected or unverified, so anyone can see what lies near their community.
strings.home.lede_html: A sourced tracker of facilities that store or destroy old or unstable energetics, starting from EPA's current open-burning / open-detonation list and a few documented comparables. 67 sites are in this cut, including Army, Navy, Air Force, Marine Corps, other DoD, Energy, NASA, and contractor facilities. It also includes 727 military installations the Department of Defense is investigating for PFAS (212 with checked map points, the rest listed by state), 1,840 EPA Superfund sites, 20 active FUSRAP nuclear cleanup sites, 72 U.S. ocean munitions dump sites, 108 DOE Legacy Management sites, 523 abandoned uranium mines on and near the Navajo Nation, 10,150 Formerly Used Defense Sites (1,493 with munitions response projects), plus region sections for Australia & New Zealand, Africa, South America, Antarctica, Arctic, Middle East and Asia, and worldwide topic pages on petroleum explosions, spills and contamination, nuclear test sites, chemical weapons and sea dumps, chemical-plant disasters, nuclear accidents and waste, firing and bombing ranges, wartime unexploded ordnance and coal-ash and tailings dam failures (see Topics). Blank fields mean no source was found — nothing here is guessed.

strings.home.nearby_intro_html: Search one ZIP code to see the closest munitions sites, military PFAS sites, Superfund cleanup sites and FUSRAP atomic-era cleanup sites. New: What is PFAS? · What is Superfund? · What is FUSRAP?
strings.home.nearby_enter: Enter a five-digit U.S. ZIP code to see the closest sites in this inventory. The map will zoom to that ZIP.
strings.home.alerts_intro: Get an email when this site records a documented incident, permit change, or public-comment deadline at a tracked munitions site, or a status change at a Formerly Used Defense Site, Superfund, FUSRAP, DOE Legacy Management, Navajo-area abandoned uranium mine, mapped military PFAS or mapped sea-dump site, within 50 miles of a U.S. ZIP code you enter, plus changes to unmapped military PFAS and sea-dump sites in or off your state. You must confirm your address by email before any alerts are sent. Distance is not a measure of risk.
strings.home.alerts_note_html: You must confirm by email before any alerts are sent. See the privacy notice for what is collected, how MailerLite is used, and how to unsubscribe.
strings.nearby.note: Distances are straight-line miles from the ZIP Code Tabulation Area (ZCTA) center published in the U.S. Census Bureau 2025 gazetteer, or from a location this browser reports after you click “Use my location.” They are not driving distance and not a measure of risk. Only sites in this dataset are included. Not every postal ZIP has a ZCTA centroid. Your location is not sent to a server.

strings.nearby.live_lede: This page collects official, public guidance for people who live, work, or go to school near a facility in this tracker. It covers 67 sites in the current cut. It does not tell you whether any one site is safe or unsafe, and it does not give medical advice.
strings.nearby.medical: This guide points to official public sources so residents can find emergency-planning contacts, permit notices, and records-request portals. It is not medical advice, legal advice, or an emergency instruction. In an emergency, follow directions from local officials. Health questions belong with a licensed clinician or the local health department. FOIA and permit comments have formal rules; agency pages control how to file.
strings.nearby.medical_not_gov: This site is published by D.A. Williams. It is not an official U.S. government document and should not be mistaken for one. For a medical question, contact a clinician or your local public health department. For an emergency, follow instructions from local officials or call 911.
